newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity mostly higher on Southwest heat.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity mostly higher on Southwest heat.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading mostly higher Thursday based on expectations for strong cooling demand in the Southwest where heat was expected to dominate through the weekend, industry sources said.
"It's hot in the Southwest, and Palo Verde is dragging COB (California Oregon Border) higher," said a New York-based futures trader.
As of 1220 EDT, NYMEX July Palo Verde (PV) was up 79 cents at $31.10 after hitting a new contract high of $32.50 and trading as low as $30.50 per megawatt hour (MWh).
August PV was up 55 cents at $32.25 after trades in a range of $32.00-32.40 per MWh.
July COB was up 21 cents at the day's low of $22.90 after reaching as high as $23.30, while August was down 18 cents at the day's low of $25.35 after reaching as high as $25.70 per MWh.
NYMEX said that as of 1140 EDT an estimated total of 93 COB and 237 PV contracts had traded.
Temperatures in the Southwest were expected to be near-normal in the northeast to about five degrees above normal in the southwest through the weekend.
Maximum temperatures in Phoenix were expected to be near 105 degrees Fahrenheit Friday, with overnight lows near 76 degrees.
Physical power prices in the West were said to have risen on the cooling demand, with next-day COB pegged at $27.50-28.00 per MWh from a Wednesday range of $25.00-27.00 per MWh.

Separately, Arizona Public Service said it expects to resume power output at its 1,221 megawatt (MW) Palo Verde 1 nuclear power unit in Arizona Thursday following the reconstruction of a charging pump.
Arizona Public Service had said it expected to restart the unit Wednesday from a weekend outage to repair a valve leak.
Also, the 1,087 MW Diablo Canyon nuclear power unit remained off line for refueling, and was expected to restart this weekend.

In addition to the Palo Verde and Diablo Canyon nukes, several units were expected to return to service by Monday, including a 750 MW unit at Colstrip in Montana, a 750 MW unit at Four Corners in Arizona, a 550 MW unit at Jim Bridger in Wyoming and a 400 MW unit at the Bonanza plant in Utah.
A total of about 3,000 MW of coal-fired generation in the West was scheduled to return to service through next week as spring maintenance was completed.
As of 1215 EDT, the July NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas contract was trading down 5.1 cents at $2.265 per million British thermal units.
Temperatures in the Pacific Northwest were expected to be three to four degrees above normal through the weekend with scattered showers primarily through the weekend.
